Application.Label: Sample application A
Application.Name: Sample application A
Application.Info: A leaf in the tree. Selecting it should set a variable.

Messages.Message: This is the UiSharp interactive self-test. Every screen tells you what to check.

Actions.Action:
Welcome.
This runs through every dialog UiSharp can show, one at a time. On each screen, check that:
- the text is readable and nothing is cut off at the edges - the buttons are reachable and hit the right size for this screen - Back and Cancel do what they say
Cancel on any screen stops the self-test. That is itself worth testing at least once.
This screen also carries two images. Check that:
- the banner across the top is fully visible and not cut off - the file is 900 pixels wide, wider than this dialog, so it has to have been scaled down - the small square below the text is animating through four colours - a still square means this boot image cannot animate a GIF - the title bar and the panel on the left both show a round blue icon
Continue when you are ready.

Action.Title: Text input
Action.Subtitle: Typing, validation and passwords
Action.InputInfo: Type into each field below. The first two are validated: the dialog should refuse to continue until they are filled in correctly, and say why.

InputText.Question: A required name (3-15 characters, letters only)
InputText.Hint: Letters only, at least three of them.

InputText.Question: A password field — the characters must not be visible
An optional note — leaving this empty must be allowed

Action.Title: Choices
Action.Subtitle: Drop-downs, defaults and check boxes
Action.InputInfo: The first drop-down should already have "Second" selected, because the configuration set a default.

InputChoice.Question: A drop-down built from a list
This choice only appears when the machine is x64

ActionGroup.Name: Navigation
ActionGroup.Action:
This screen is inside an action group, and it is not the first dialog of the run — so a Back button should be offered.
Press Back, confirm you land on the previous screen with your answers still filled in, then come forward again.

This is the second dialog in the same group.
Back from here should return to the previous screen rather than leaving the group.

Action.Title: Preflight checks
Action.Subtitle: Passing, warning and failing checks side by side

Check.WarnDescription: A warning should look different from a failure, and should not block continuing.

Check.ErrorDescription: This one is meant to fail. Confirm the failure is obvious and that this text is readable.

Check.Text: This machine reports at least 1 GB of memory
Check.WarnDescription: Under 4 GB reported (%XHWMemory% MB) — fine for a self-test, worth noticing on real hardware.

Actions.Action: This is the error dialog, shown deliberately. It should be visibly an error — not just an ordinary information screen with different words — and it should offer no way to continue past it other than acknowledging it. It takes the same banner as the welcome screen, and renders the same markup the information screens do: that word should be bold rather than showing its tags.

This screen should cover the whole display, with nothing of the desktop or of WinPE visible behind it.
The banner should be centred near the top, scaled to the screen rather than to the dialog it was scaled to earlier.
It also has a timeout: if nothing is pressed it continues on its own after twenty seconds, counting down as it goes. Watch the countdown rather than pressing anything, so the timeout is tested too.

Action.Title: Missing images
Action.Subtitle: A failure that must not be fatal

Actions.Action:
This screen asks for two images that cannot be loaded: one file that does not exist, and one URL that cannot be reached.
Both should be missing, this text should be exactly where it would be if no images had been asked for, and the log should carry a warning naming each one. What must not happen is the dialog failing to appear.
The URL will take a few seconds to give up. That wait is the point: it is what a boot image does when the network is not up yet.

Every dialog was shown. What you entered:
Name %SelfTestName% Note %SelfTestNote% Choice %SelfTestChoice% List choice %SelfTestList% Check box %SelfTestCheckbox%
What the machine reported:
WinPE %XOSWinPE% Architecture %XOSArchitecture% Chassis %XHWChassisType% Manufacturer %XHWManufacturer% Model %XHWModel% Serial %XHWSerialNumber% Memory (MB) %XHWMemory% UEFI %XSystemUEFI%
Everything above was written to:
%SelfTestFile%
If any screen looked wrong, that file plus the UiSharp log is what to attach to the report.
The password you typed was cleared before anything was written, so it appears in neither.
